problems.problem: D3 LEAK IN THE SPEC'S OWN SQL. In §9 search_all(), the eligibility filters are applied inconsistently across the three RRF legs. The `fts` CTE has `promoted_at IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('open','dormant') AND coinability_tier <> 'never'`. The `trg` CTE has only `coinability_tier <> 'never'`. The `vec` CTE has NEITHER — its WHERE clause is `search_vec IS NOT NULL`, full stop. A story tiered 'never' (identifiable private individual, a death, a minor) is retrievable by the vector leg and, because RRF is a UNION ALL fusion, it enters the result set. §3's claim that tier='never' is 'hard-filtered BEFORE ranking, not down-weighted' is contradicted by the query shape shipped in the same document. The No-coin-yet chip query does get this right, which makes the search path the exposed one.
problems.fix: Hoist eligibility into a single `eligible_narratives` CTE (promoted_at NOT NULL, status IN ('open','dormant'), coinability_tier <> 'never') and have all three legs join it, rather than repeating a filter list per leg. Same for the post and coin variants — a post's eligibility must be inherited from its narrative, which the spec never states. Add a CI test that seeds one tier='never' story and asserts zero rows from search_all for a query matching its embedding but not its title.

problems.problem: LOOKUP FAILURE IS RENDERED AS A CONFIDENT NEGATIVE VERDICT. The CA ladder rung 5 renders 'Valid Solana address. No pair, no story, no post.' and the $TICKER verdict header renders '$FERRY is free on Solana — you'd be first.' Both are reached when the upstream lookup returns nothing. But lib/token-lookup.js returns `{found:false}` for at least four distinct reasons that are indistinguishable to the caller: genuinely absent, DexScreener non-200 (throws, caught in api/token-lookup.js:24 into `{found:false, error}`), no Solana pair yet, and — critically — `mapped.liquidity <= 0` (lines 153 and 171). At step 6 of the build order the $TICKER screen runs entirely on this path with no coin_index behind it. A DexScreener 429 on a hot ticker therefore renders 'you'd be first to deploy it' and a full-width primary Create button. The product's single anti-duplicate promise inverts into instructing the user to mint the duplicate, under load, exactly when the ticker is hottest.
problems.fix: Add a fourth verdict state and a fourth CA-ladder terminus: UNKNOWN. Any non-200, timeout, or rate-limit from DexScreener must surface as 'We couldn't check whether $FERRY exists right now' with Create SUPPRESSED, not demoted. Change lib/token-lookup.js to return a discriminated `{status:'found'|'absent'|'unavailable'}` instead of a boolean `found`, and stop conflating `liquidity <= 0` with absence — a zero-liquidity mint is a coin that exists and is the exact case the anti-duplicate screen must catch.

problems.problem: THE $TICKER FAMILY TABLE CAN RENDER TWO BUY BUTTONS SIDE BY SIDE. Per-row action: "'Buy' only on rows with match_status='confirmed' or 'adopted'". match_status lives on narrative_tickers and is scoped per (narrative, mint). Two unrelated narratives can each have a CONFIRMED coin whose symbol is FERRY — §5.2's own data shows PUMP has 4 distinct mints and MOON 6, and nothing in the matcher enforces symbol uniqueness across narratives. The screen whose entire job is 'so the user buys instead of minting the fourth copy' then presents two equally-styled solid-cyan Buy buttons with no disambiguation. The ONE RULE is defined per-story; this screen is per-symbol, and the spec never resolves the scope mismatch. The verdict header even anticipates the case — '$FERRY exists 4 times. 1 is matched to a story' — but has no sentence for 'exists 4 times, 2 are matched to different stories'.
problems.fix: Define the symbol-scoped rule explicitly: if confirmed-across-all-narratives for this symbol is >1, NO row gets a Buy — every row gets View, and the verdict header reads '$FERRY exists 4 times. 2 are matched to different stories — we can't tell you which one you mean.' Add that as a fifth verdict sentence and a fifth screen state. This is the ONE RULE's 'two or more → See the N' applied at symbol scope, which is where the copycat risk actually lives.

problems.problem: BUY HAS NO SAFETY OR LIVENESS GATE OUTSIDE THE JUST-MADE CHIP. Safety appears exactly once in the spec, on the Just made / Trending screen ('Buy is replaced by a red-outlined Risky pill when a hard safety gate trips'). The same Buy button, keyed off the same confirmed count, also appears on: the free-text story row, the BEST MATCH strip, the Coin row, the CA identity card, the $TICKER family table, the Following sections 1/3/4, and the mint toast. None of them consults api/safety.js. Worse, match_status='confirmed' is an identity assertion, not a tradeability assertion — it never expires. A confirmed coin that has since been rugged to zero liquidity renders 'Buy $FERRY' forever, because nothing in the spec re-evaluates it. The old `tradeable()` in lib/types.ts at least incidentally checked `mcap != null`; replacing it with `match_status === 'confirmed'` (build step 2) removes even that accident.
problems.fix: Make the primary-button resolver a two-input function: confirmed identity AND current tradeability (liquidity > 0, no hard safety gate per §4.4's five conditions, price data fresher than N minutes). Put it in one module — features/search/model/action.ts — that every one of the eight surfaces calls, and enumerate a 'confirmed but not currently tradeable' state (Risky pill / 'liquidity gone') as a first-class state on every screen that renders Buy, not just Just made.

problems.problem: FEES ARE INVISIBLE ON EVERY BUY SURFACE, INCLUDING ONE-TAP-FROM-PUSH. docs/DESIGN.md §295 states Insidor sets its own integrator fee (max 255 bps) and api/swap.js already forwards feeAccount; §299 flags that Jupiter's own platform fee on sub-24h tokens is unresolved (docs say 50 bps, live API returned 10 bps) — and every Insidor trade is on a sub-24h token. The spec renders Buy in eight places and never mentions fee, slippage, or price impact once. The mint toast is the sharpest version: 'Buy opens the Jupiter modal in place, no navigation — every navigation between the alert and the buy costs seconds.' That is a deliberately friction-minimised path from an OS push notification to a fee-bearing trade on a minutes-old token, with the fee never named. The brief's honest-record axis is explicit that fees must be legible, and D2's logic ('if a user must opt in to seeing misses, the record is marketing') applies identically to cost.
problems.fix: Add a fee line to the trade entry point wherever it appears, at the same weight as the lead-time line: mono 10px 'Insidor fee 0.85% · Jupiter 0.10% · est. impact 2.3%' sourced from the /order quote response, rendered BEFORE the confirm, including inside the toast-mounted panel. If the toast cannot render it, the toast falls back to navigation — the 400ms saved is not worth an undisclosed fee on a push-driven trade.

problems.problem: ANONYMOUS FOLLOWERS GET NO NOTIFICATION, AND THE DEDUPE KEY IS BROKEN FOR THEM. The ★ is specced as wallet-free and account-free via follow.device_id, and the flow doc's promise ('You do not need a wallet to do that') is quoted as justification. But §8's enqueue writes `INSERT INTO notification (...) SELECT ... FROM follow WHERE narrative_id = ...` and then broadcasts to `'user:'||user_id`. For a device-only follow, user_id is NULL: (a) the Broadcast topic is 'user:' — no toast, no realtime; (b) dedupe_key = `user_id || ':' || narrative_id || ':' || ...` evaluates to NULL because concatenation with NULL yields NULL in Postgres, so the UNIQUE index never conflicts (NULL is never equal to NULL) and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` never fires — every re-run inserts another row, unbounded; (c) the while-you-were-away band's query is specced as `WHERE read_at IS NULL AND created_at > last_session_end` with no device_id predicate. Separately, `date_trunc('hour', now())/6` is a type error — you cannot divide timestamptz by integer.
problems.fix: dedupe_key = coalesce(user_id::text, 'dev:'||device_id) || ':' || narrative_id || ':' || floor(extract(epoch from now())/21600)::text, with a NOT NULL constraint on the column so this can never regress silently. Broadcast topic becomes coalesce('user:'||user_id, 'device:'||device_id) and the client subscribes to its device topic when anonymous. Add device_id to the band query. Then add an explicit state to the notification screen: 'anonymous follower, notification fires' — currently the highest-volume follower class has no specced delivery path at all.

problems.problem: story_outcome.peak_mcap HAS NO DATA SOURCE, WHICH MAKES THE FINISHED CHIP AND THE FOLLOW-UP RULE UNBUILDABLE. The materialized view is specced with peak_mcap, and outcome ∈ ('early','late','flat','no_coin','unresolved') where FLAT is defined as 'a coin existed but peaked under $50k'. Peak requires a market-cap time series per mint. post_snapshots is post engagement only (views/likes/retweets/replies/quotes/bookmarks — verified in docs/schema.md). coin_index as specced holds a scalar mcap plus updated_at, i.e. last-observed, not peak. No coin_snapshots table appears anywhere in the dataContract or the build order. The same missing series kills the notification follow-up rule ('a later coin's peak mcap > 4× the first AND the first peaked under $25k') and makes openQuestion #5 ('is $50k the right EARLY/FLAT boundary') unanswerable, since the column it would tune does not exist. Build step 13 lists story_outcome as buildable once the two clocks land; it is not.
problems.fix: Add coin_snapshots (mint, captured_at, mcap, liquidity, price, vol24h) to the MISSING—NEW TABLES list and to build step 13 BEFORE story_outcome, with a sampling cadence stated (the geometric grid used for posts is the obvious reuse). Until it exists, story_outcome must emit only 'early' | 'late' | 'no_coin' | 'unresolved' and the Finished chip must omit both the Peak mcap column and the FLAT outcome chip rather than render a last-observed value labelled 'peak'.

problems.problem: THE BEST MATCH STRIP HAS NO ACTION RULE FOR A COIN WITH NO STORY. §4(c) lifts 'the single highest-scoring object of any kind' into a strip 'resolved to exactly one action', and typePrior gives coins 0.95 — so a coin frequently wins, especially on a $TICKER-shaped query where the ×1.35 exact-ticker boost fires on coin_index.symbol. But the primary button is only ever defined as 'a pure function of how many CONFIRMED coins a STORY has'. For a coin object with match_status='no story' (the majority of coin_index), confirmed_coin_count is undefined. The spec's silence means the obvious implementation renders Buy — putting a one-tap purchase of a completely unprovenanced mint at the top of the results page, in a 72px hero strip, which is precisely the DexScreener behaviour the product exists to beat.
problems.fix: State the coin-object rule explicitly and make it restrictive: a coin resolves to Buy only when match_status ∈ ('confirmed','adopted') AND its symbol has no competing confirmed mint; a NO STORY or UNVERIFIED coin resolves to 'View' with the MATCH stamp inline. Better still: suppress the BEST MATCH strip entirely when the winner is a coin with no story — the strip's stated reason string ('exact ticker match') is not an answer to 'is this the real one', which is the question the whole feature claims to answer.

problems.problem: THE MINT TOAST CAN RENDER A STALE PRIMARY BUTTON. Coalescing is a 90-second window from the first confirm. The toast auto-dismisses at 12s but pauses on hover and 'never auto-dismisses while the Jupiter modal it opened is on screen'. So a toast reading 'Buy $CUPS' can be on-screen — with a trade panel open — at t+95s when a second coin confirms and confirmed_coin_count moves 1→2. The spec has no re-resolution rule for a rendered toast, so the forbidden 'buy which one?' state is rendered in the single highest-stakes surface in the product, on the exact copycat-swarm timeline the coalescing window was designed for (§8 says swarms mint 3–8 coins in under a minute, which means the tail of a swarm routinely lands past 90s).
problems.fix: Make the toast a live subscriber to confirmed_coin_count for its narrative for as long as it is mounted, not a snapshot. On 1→2 while mounted, the primary button re-resolves to 'See the 3 coins' with a 240ms amber flash and a one-line 'another coin just appeared'. If a Jupiter panel is already open when this fires, do not swap the button silently — surface the warning above the panel. Add 'second coin confirms while toast is live' to the notification screen's state list.

problems.problem: THE RANKING FORMULA DOUBLE-PENALISES AGE AND NEVER USES LEAD TIME. §3 sets score = 0.55·rel + 0.25·vir + 0.20·rec, where vir = ln(1+heat)/ln(101) and heat is the §4.2 presented heat. But §4.2 (line 444) defines heat = (base·O·D)^0.85 / ((age_min+12)/12)^1.35 × C — heat is ALREADY age-decayed, and line 460 says presented heat is additionally p95-normalised to 0..100. So `vir` takes an already-normalised, already-age-penalised quantity, logs it (a second compression), and then `rec` applies a third, independent age decay. A 90-minute story is penalised roughly three times over. More importantly for the thesis: lead_time and t_crypto appear nowhere in the ranking, in any boost, or in any sort or filter on the search surface. The one quantity that is the product — 'crypto has not seen this yet', which the No-coin-yet Lead cell itself calls 'the best possible state' — is a passive badge you cannot rank, sort, or filter by anywhere in this feature.
problems.fix: Drop `rec` entirely (heat carries recency) and replace it with an earliness term: ×1.20 boost when t_crypto IS NULL (crypto has not touched this), ×1.10 when lead_time_min > 20. Make the Lead column sortable on every table that renders it, and add a sixth chip — 'Crypto hasn't seen it' — filtering on t_crypto IS NULL. Without that chip the search surface is a well-built generic crypto screener that would look identical shipped by a company with no detection pipeline.

problems.problem: THE FOLLOW ONLY FIRES ON THE MOMENT THE HEAD START IS SPENT. The thesis is a 20–90 minute lead over crypto. The notification trigger is confirmed_coin_count 0→≥1 — i.e. it fires when the coin exists, which is t=0 of the race everyone else is already in. The spec calls this 'the retention hook the whole feature exists to deliver' and budgets p50 < 20s to it. That reframes the product from 'be first to the story' to 'be 20 seconds fast to the mint', which is what Axiom and Photon already do. The alert that would actually serve the thesis — 'your watched story is accelerating' or 'crypto Twitter just picked this up (t_ct fired), the window is closing' — does not exist. notify_mint's three values are all/mint_only/muted, and 'all' is defined as 'every coin, every reopen': coin events only, all three of them.
problems.fix: Add a pre-coin notification kind to the notification table and to notify_mint: 'accelerating' (heat_rank crosses into the top N, or accel > threshold, throttled to one per story) and 'window closing' (t_ct becomes non-null while confirmed_coin_count is still 0 — crypto found your story and there is still no coin). The second one is the single most on-thesis alert the product can send and it is the one that drives Create, which is the path with no fee-disclosure problem and no copycat risk.

problems.problem: THE HONEST-RECORD HEADLINE HAS AN UNDECLARED DENOMINATOR AND HIDES THE NORMAL ABSTAIN RATE. The Finished summary band reads 'Stories 214 · Early 61% · median +23m · Late 34% · median −7m'. 61 + 34 = 95, so either no_coin/flat/unresolved are 5% of 214 (implausible — most viral stories never mint) or the percentages are over a coin-having subset while the '214' beside them is the full count. The spec never says which. On the one screen whose entire purpose is auditability, the headline number is ambiguous. Separately, the abstain-rate note is conditional: it only appears 'when UNRESOLVED > 30% of the window'. §5.7 sets the expected operating abstain band at 15–30%, so at normal operation the user is never told that roughly a quarter of matches are abstained — the disclosure appears only when things are abnormal, which is the inverse of D2.
problems.fix: Make the denominator explicit in the band: 'Stories 214 · got a coin 71% · never did 29%' as the first row, then 'Of the 152 that got a coin: early 61%, late 34%, flat 5%'. Move the abstain line from conditional to permanent: a fourth stat cell 'Abstained 22%' in the same weight as the others, with the amber warning treatment reserved for >30%.

problems.problem: THE COMPONENT-REUSE CLAIM IS FALSE, AND .sr-narr IS REDEFINED UNDER ITS OWN NAME. priorArt states 'Exactly two components are new: .match-stamp and .sr-post.' Checked against docs/research/design-component-inventory.md: neither .match-stamp nor .sr-post appears there (0 hits each), which is consistent — but so are the BEST MATCH strip, the verdict header band, the collision line, the resolution trace, the mode chip, the chip rail with live counts, the ticker-family 10-column grid, the Finished summary band, the Finished 10-column record table, the while-you-were-away band, the two-button toast action row, the 3-state bell, the Not-mintable pill, the MINT IN POST tag, and the Graduating progress cell. That is ~15 new components, not two. Worse, inventory line 220 defines `.sr-narr` as `grid-template-columns:56px 1fr` — a thumb and one text column. The spec redefines it as `28px 56px minmax(0,1.9fr) .7fr .6fr .8fr 132px`. That is a different component wearing an existing class name; shipped alongside the prototype CSS it produces a live selector collision.
problems.fix: Rename the extended row to .sr-narr-row (or .ttr-narr) and leave .sr-narr alone. Then rewrite the priorArt claim as an honest inventory: list the ~15 new components explicitly, because 'we reuse everything' is exactly the sentence that gets a design review waved through and then costs three weeks.

problems.problem: THE MIGRATION-A PREMISE IS UNVERIFIED AND MAY CREATE A DUPLICATE COLUMN. The dataContract calls narrative_tickers.mint 'THE hard blocker' and says 'docs/schema.md lists mint_ca; the real catalog does not have it.' But docs/schema.md line 63 does list mint_ca, and the file's own header (line 3) says it was generated from a 'Supabase service probe (SELECT * LIMIT 1) + schema SQL fallback' — a live probe. So either the probe saw the column (it exists, possibly unpopulated) or the probe fell through to the SQL fallback for this table. The spec asserts the second without evidence. Every screen in the feature and all 15 build steps sit downstream of this one migration, and the spec proposes a NEW column named `mint` rather than using or renaming `mint_ca` — if mint_ca does exist, the result is two columns for one concept and two code paths reading them.
problems.fix: Before writing Migration A, run an actual information_schema query against the live catalog and paste the result into the spec. If mint_ca exists, rename it (ALTER ... RENAME COLUMN) rather than adding `mint`; if it does not, fix docs/schema.md and the generator that produced it, because a schema doc that hallucinates columns will do it again on the next twelve.

problems.problem: THREE SPECCED STATES ARE UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE API THE SPEC NAMES. (a) lib/token-lookup.js lines 153 and 171: both lookupTicker and lookupMint return `{found:false}` when `mapped.liquidity <= 0`. The state 'brand-new mint, no market data — every numeric —, Buy still enabled (it is a valid bonding-curve buy)' is therefore unreachable via /api/token-lookup?mint=, which is named as CA-ladder rung 3. (b) mapPair lines 82–86 coerce mcap, vol24h, liquidity and priceUsd to 0 via `|| 0`, so the rule 'never 0 and never a green chip' requires changing mapPair to null-preserving — which changes the response shape consumed by site/live.js, site/tokenpage.js and components/StoryCard.tsx, and is not in the build order. (c) rung 3 is required to yield mint_time = min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL pairs, but the endpoint returns ageMin computed by ageMinFromPair(pickBestPair(...)) — one pair, and a relative minute count with no absolute timestamp field at all. Build step 5 says it ships 'with the existing /api/token-lookup?mint= as rung 3'; it cannot.
problems.fix: Add an explicit build step 0.5: rework lib/token-lookup.js to (i) return null rather than 0 for every absent numeric, (ii) return mintTime as an absolute timestamp computed as min(pairCreatedAt) over all Solana pairs, (iii) stop treating liquidity<=0 as not-found and return a `hasMarket:false` flag instead, (iv) return a discriminated status per the rate-limit fix above. Then update the three existing consumers. This is ~60 lines and it gates five screens; it is not a detail of step 5.

problems.problem: ts_headline OUTPUT IS INJECTED AS HTML OVER ARBITRARY SOCIAL TEXT. §5 specifies StartSel=, StopSel= and the result is rendered with styling. ts_headline does not escape HTML in the source document — it wraps matched lexemes and returns the surrounding source text verbatim. narrative_posts.text is arbitrary user-generated content scraped from X and TikTok. Rendering that string in React requires dangerouslySetInnerHTML, at which point a post containing `` executes in the context of a page that holds a Privy session and can initiate swaps. The spec mentions sanitisation nowhere, on a surface whose entire content is untrusted third-party text.
problems.fix: Do not return HTML from Postgres. Use StartSel/StopSel with sentinel tokens that cannot occur in social text (e.g. /), escape the fragment client-side, then split on the sentinels and render <mark> as real React elements. Add a unit test in features/search/model/ that feeds a post containing a script tag through the snippet path and asserts no raw HTML reaches the DOM.

problems.problem: DENSITY DRIFT: FOUR BESPOKE FULL-WIDTH BANDS AND A THREE-LINE ROW CELL. The inventory's row baseline is `min-height:54px; padding:13px 20px`. The spec adds a 72px BEST MATCH strip, a 64px verdict band, a 96px Finished summary band, an 88px while-you-were-away band, and a 56px-tall search input with radius 13 — each 1.5–2 rows tall and none in the inventory. The story row then stacks title (Clash 14px) over an 18-word ts_headline snippet over platform marks in one cell, which cannot render inside 54px; realistically ~80px. With a 72px strip, three section headers, and ≤6 story rows at ~80px, the first viewport shows roughly six results. A screener shows twenty. The Following screen's centered max-width:480px teaching empty state is a consumer onboarding card dropped into a terminal.
problems.fix: Collapse the BEST MATCH strip into a normal-height row with a 2px cyan left edge and a right-aligned button — the left edge already carries the 'this is the answer' signal without a hero. Clamp the story row snippet to one line at 11.5px and drop the platform marks into the thumb corner. Target 54–60px rows and 12+ visible results above the fold at 900px viewport height, and state that as a numeric acceptance criterion in the spec.

problems.problem: NO RETRACTION PATH WHEN A CONFIRMED MATCH IS LATER REJECTED. match_status is a mutable column and §5.7 describes ongoing calibration and monthly refreshed eval sets, so confirmed→rejected and confirmed→unsure will both occur in production. The spec covers unsure→confirmed in detail (in-app only, no push, honest lead) but has no state, no notification, and no row treatment for a match being withdrawn after the user was pushed 'Wrong Name is now $CUPS' and possibly bought. The trigger in §8 fires only on the transition INTO 'confirmed'.
problems.fix: Add a 'retracted' notification kind and a row state. If a narrative_tickers row leaves 'confirmed' and the user has a delivered notification for it, fire an in-app correction ('we were wrong about $CUPS — it is not from this story') and mark the original notification row corrected_at. Show the correction in the while-you-were-away band. A product that publishes its misses (D2) cannot silently un-publish its false positives.

problems.problem: A HELD QUIET-HOURS NOTIFICATION RENDERS A FIRE-TIME EARLINESS CLAIM AS CURRENT. State: 'fired, quiet hours → held, delivered as the first band on next open, with a dim held during quiet hours'. The band content is the toast content, whose line 2 is 'Minted 2m ago · $18.4K · you're 31m early' — all three values computed at fire time. Delivered eight hours later, 'minted 2m ago' is false, '$18.4K' is a stale mcap presented without any staleness treatment, and '31m early' describes a window that closed overnight. The spec's own argument ('a 5-minute notification on a product that sells 20-minute head starts is worth nothing') applies with far more force here.
problems.fix: Recompute every numeric at render time in the band, never replay the payload. Held items render 'Minted 8h ago · $4.1K now (was $18.4K) · we told you 31m before crypto, 8h ago'. And state a general rule the spec is missing: coin market numbers carry a freshness treatment everywhere they appear — the .live-dot is currently specced only on the CA identity card, so every mcap in every table renders identically whether it is 2 seconds or 40 minutes old.

problems.problem: THE CONFIRMED-COIN RANKING BOOST IS AN UNDISCLOSED THUMB ON THE SCALE. §3 applies ×1.05 because 'story has ≥1 CONFIRMED coin (an actionable result is a better result)'. The actionable result is the one that produces an integrator fee (DESIGN.md §295); the Create path produces none. It is a small coefficient and a defensible product argument, but it is a revenue-correlated relevance adjustment on a surface the spec elsewhere insists must not reorder by popularity ('a search box that reorders your query by popularity is a trending board wearing a search box'). Same reasoning applies.
problems.fix: Either drop it, or keep it and disclose it in the same place the ranking is otherwise explained — one mono 10px line in the .tbar-meta on /search: 'results with a tradeable coin rank slightly higher'. Then measure it in search_log; if click-through does not justify 1.05, it was a fee preference wearing a relevance coefficient.

problems.problem: HOLDERS-PER-ROW IS A HELIUS RPC CALL PER VISIBLE ROW. The $TICKER family table and the Just made table both carry a Holders column, sourced 'from api/holders.js, lazily per visible row'. api/holders.js is a Helius getTokenAccounts call, paginated, keyed on a single mint, with a per-mint in-process cache that does not survive across serverless instances. On the Just made table with a From-a-story-only toggle that can be switched off to a ~40k/day firehose, lazy-per-visible-row means one paginated RPC per row per scroll, on a shared Helius key.
problems.fix: Move holders into the coin_index indexer as a periodically refreshed column with a captured_at, and render it with an age treatment. If it must be live, batch it: one endpoint accepting up to 25 mints, called once per rendered page, with a stated stale-while-revalidate window. Also drop the Holders column from Just made entirely — a 90-second-old token's holder count is 3 and tells the user nothing.

problems.problem: THE SPECCED FILE PATHS AND SQL DO NOT MATCH THE REPOSITORY OR COMPILE. (a) features/search/model/parse.ts and the apps/web monorepo layout do not exist — the repo is flat (app/, lib/, api/, worker/, site/) with no npm workspaces in package.json. (b) parseQuery calls bs58.decode; bs58 is not a dependency. (c) In search_all, the `fts` CTE names its rank column `rnk` but `trg` and `vec` do not alias theirs, so they emit `row_number`; the outer `SUM(w / (60 + rnk))` cannot resolve `rnk` for two of three branches. (d) `vec` has both a window-function ORDER BY and a statement-level ORDER BY ... LIMIT 100, which is not the shape that gets an HNSW index scan. (e) Two spec citations point at the wrong file: `refreshWatchStars()` and `PENDING{}` are in site/index.html (2670, 1346), not live.js; and the gain_24h fallback `combined_views * 0.14` is site/index.html:1668, not live.js:1662 (which is an Anthropic-budget message). The spec also misses a SECOND invented fallback on the line above it — a searchSeries delta — feeding the same narrViralGain24h function.
problems.fix: Fix the aliases and the vec CTE, add bs58 to dependencies, correct the four citations, and add the searchSeries fallback to the REMOVED/DO-NOT-USE list alongside the 0.14 one. Either create the workspace structure as build step 0 or restate the paths against the flat layout — the spec currently reads as though the monorepo already exists.

missing: FIRST-RUN / NORMIE STATE ON /search. The brief names three users; the spec designs for exactly one. A first-time visitor landing on /search sees the No-coin-yet chip by default: a 9-column table of unfamiliar stories with a $TICKER column, a velocity column, a lead badge, and a one-tap Create button — with no explanation of any of it. The 'normie who saw something on TikTok' has a Create button one click away and no idea what a ticker is. There is no first-run state, no column explanation affordance, and no 'search what you saw on TikTok' framing anywhere in the feature.
'WE COULDN'T CHECK' AS A DISTINCT STATE, on both the CA screen and the $TICKER verdict header. Every failure mode currently collapses into a confident negative.
CONFIRMED-BUT-NOT-CURRENTLY-TRADEABLE (rugged, liquidity drained, safety gate tripped) on the seven Buy surfaces outside Just made.
MATCH RETRACTION (confirmed → unsure/rejected after a notification was delivered and possibly acted on).
SYMBOL-SCOPED AMBIGUITY on the $TICKER screen: two mints confirmed to two different narratives. No verdict sentence, no button rule.
SECOND COIN CONFIRMS WHILE A TOAST IS MOUNTED (past the 90s coalescing window).
PRE-COIN ALERTS. No 'your story is accelerating' and no 't_ct just fired, the window is closing' — the two alerts that actually serve a 20–90 minute head start.
DATA-FRESHNESS TREATMENT on market numbers outside the CA identity card. Every mcap/liq/price in every table renders identically at 2 seconds and 40 minutes old.
ANONYMOUS-FOLLOWER DELIVERY PATH. Device follows are first-class in the ★ spec and absent from the notification spec.

ABUSE / RATE LIMITING. Unauthenticated device_id follows are unbounded row creation; no cap per device, no cap on follows per narrative. Same for the search path, which fans out to DexScreener on arbitrary uncached queries.

STORY THAT AGES OUT OF THE SEARCHABLE SET. openQuestion #9 raises it and leaves it open: a two-week-old story searched by name returns nothing and reads as a bug. That is a state, not a question — it needs a 'this story is closed, see it in Finished' result row.

SHOW-RISKY RECONCILIATION. §4.3 of the system design says risky coins are HIDDEN unless a loud showRisky toggle is on; the spec instead shows them with a Risky pill and never provides the toggle. One of the two is wrong and the spec does not say which.

EMPTY / DEGRADED VECTOR LEG. narratives.search_vec is a centroid over post_embeddings, but the corpus is ~1,718 posts across ~1,041 narratives — many narratives have zero or one embedded post, so the third RRF leg silently covers only part of the corpus. No state, no fallback, no disclosure.
